tools.name: search_space_jobs
tools.description: Look up open roles across the space industry (launch providers, satellite and spacecraft makers, and the suppliers behind them), gathered from the job boards of 136 employers. Each result gives the title, employer, kind of work, posted pay, the countries it accepts applicants from and an apply link

tools.name: get_space_jobs_pay
tools.description: Current pay in the space industry for each kind of work, as a year's pay (an hourly posting counts at 2,080 hours), taken from the pay posted on open roles: the median, the middle half (25th to 75th percentile), and the number of posted figures and employers behind each. A figure appears only where

tools.name: get_space_jobs_market
tools.description: Counts of space industry openings: the total open now, the number first listed over the past 7 days, and breakdowns by kind of work and by employer (each employer comes with the slug search_space_jobs accepts). Pass a country to count only roles that accept applicants from it.

tools.name: get_hiring_radar
tools.description: Hiring radar is the investor dataset from SpaceJobs.Now. It holds every space industry role seen on an employer's own job board from the first time that board was read: a row per role (posted pay, field, eligible countries, opening and closing dates), daily figures per employer, and a change log. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_space_jobs_pay · Private data: get_hiring_radar · Public sink: get_space_jobs_pay.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_space_jobs_pay · Private data: get_hiring_radar · Public sink: get_space_jobs_pay

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
